settings.heading: PLA
settings.body: Precise and easy to print well — a strong default for prototypes, models, and indoor products.

settings.heading: PETG
settings.body: Tougher and more temperature-tolerant — suited to functional parts that get handled or used outdoors.

settings.heading: Currently offered
settings.body: FDM 3D printing in PLA and PETG — prototyping, small-batch runs, design support, and replacement parts.

settings.heading: Needs project review
settings.body: Fine detail, unusual geometries, and borderline parts are assessed per project — we say so before work starts, not after.

settings.heading: Not currently supported
settings.body: Resin, CNC, injection molding, additional materials, and guaranteed tolerances or lead times aren’t offered yet — this list grows only as new capabilities become real.

settings.heading: What’s offered, what needs review, what’s not supported.

settings.question: How smooth will the surface be?
settings.answer: Layer lines are part of FDM — orientation and settings minimize them where it matters. We’ll show you what to expect before printing. Specimen answer.

settings.question: PLA or PETG — how do you decide?
settings.answer: By how the part lives: indoors and precise favors PLA; handled, flexed, or outdoors favors PETG. The quote explains the recommendation. Specimen answer.

settings.heading: Not sure if it fits? Ask.
settings.body: Describe the part and how it’ll be used — we’ll tell you honestly whether our process is right for it.
settings.caption: No commitment — a quote is a conversation, not a contract.
